## SECTION 4 — VALUATION ENGINE & CASH-FLOW DEFINITION

**Engine selected: 10-year discounted-cash-flow (FCFF-equivalent) on Adjusted Free Cash Flow = OCF − capex − SBC, with half-year convention and Gordon terminal value.**

Why this engine and definition:
1. A multiple approach (P/E or EV/EBITDA) is dangerous here because the margin structure is still inflecting (op margin 19.6% → 25%+ guided trajectory); trailing multiples embed a stale margin.
2. The pack's own warning requires subtracting SBC from OCF-based owner earnings. Failure to subtract SBC overstates FCF by ~$0.16B/yr (~3.4% of revenue) and adds ~$10–$12 per share to a "naive FCF" valuation.
3. I do **not** build FCF from an EBIT−tax−capex−D&A−ΔWC component model: the pack lacks the full OCF bridge (deferred taxes, other non-cash, cash-flow-statement WC vs. balance-sheet WC), and a component model underpredicts realized FY2025 FCF by ~$0.46B. I instead anchor on **realized cash conversion**, which has averaged wide margins (10–25% of revenue) with an upward trend.

Net cash bridge: Cash+ST securities $1.947B [10-Q] − LT convertible notes $1.24B [10-Q, principal] − finance leases $0.060B [FY25 Filed] = **net cash +$0.65B** (operating leases $0.095B excluded; vendor "total debt" $1.39B may include them — the discrepancy is acknowledged in §10).
